A heterogeneous union has a key only when every two of its arms, those of one heading group included, fix different literals on a key column (logical/props.ts unionProps), and the page compiler refuses a heterogeneous union without one (logical/order.ts). So the arms of a paged heading group are pairwise disjoint, and UNION ALL over them delivers what UNION does; a group of overlapping arms is refused before this code runs.

simplify.test.ts: a conjunct whose left variable is another's right (acct = third after account = acct) becomes a region equality of its own.
simplify.test.ts: a conjunct whose right variable is another's left (fourthAccount = account) reaches samePair's reversed comparison and stays.

Without the check, R03 also removes an occurrence binding only some of the containment's target fields, each matched to the referring occurrence's variable. Every node is a set, and the containment gives every referring row a target row agreeing on all its fields, hence on those bound, so the occurrence remains a pure existence test the containment discharges and the region's set is unchanged.

derivedMigrationName (deploy/render/naming.ts) never reads one change twice: a theory field's column and a manifest column object (a stored tag's) are never the same column, and no identity is added, dropped, changed or retired at once, so leaving out the deduplication, or keying it by identity alone, names the same changes.
A non-associative operator's left operand (sql/print.ts) parenthesized from two levels up instead of one: only more parentheses, which PostgreSQL reads to the same tree.

A connective's or construct's operand count (lower/conservative/expr/ops.ts): the validated DAG gives AND, OR, LEAST and GREATEST at least one operand, NOT one and BETWEEN three, so the count tests never decide.

A connective's or construct's operand count (lower/conservative/expr/ops.ts): the validated DAG gives AND, OR, LEAST and GREATEST at least one operand, NOT one and BETWEEN three, so the count tests never decide.

isPureState without its data test (check/recursion/termination.ts): counter() runs only for a term that reads state, and a counter term's operands are the state variable and a literal, so a state variable a data match also binds makes the term read nothing and form() returns data before counter() looks.
A refusal's wording (check/checker.ts MissingDiscriminant): which of two phrases explains the missing discriminant; the reason and location are unchanged.

Order completion without its fixed test (check/checker.ts complete): a column the attachment's correlation fixes holds one value across each parent's child rows, so appending it as a key changes no order.

sameKeySets always false (logical/annotate.ts) restates a Base over a view whose stamped keys already equal the view's: the rebuilt node carries the same primary key, keys and claims, a new node of identical content, so no reading of the DAG changes.

pairLaw (analysis/theory/fill.ts) is read only for a fold plane's pair on the predecessor axis, whose from is the plane's before: a law column only that plane carries, or an accumulated field, which Namings.refuseMisnamed (theory/families.ts) refuses when a second statement fills it, so no other pair of the axis has that from and the from alone picks the pair.

A contract law's sides (analysis/theory/laws.ts contract) are read only for their relations (theory.ts #dependencies): its name is its contract's alone (theory.ts contractStatement) and its native the contract's domain (laws/model/plan.ts), so the terms of each side change nothing.

finish's attribute filter (logical/props.ts) drops nothing: every caller hands it dependencies over the node's own attributes, carried renaming each input attribute to a delivered column or to a hidden attribute the caller lists (hiddenOf, keptRest), a region its sources' attributes, each bound or hidden, so keeping every dependency changes no closure.

Without the shortcut (logical/props.ts regionProps givenBy), a determinant's column the source fixes is given by its hidden attribute or a bound member of its class; determinantsOf lists the empty determinant first, whose dependency from the region's lateral reads alone reaches every column the source fixes, so the longer from is reached exactly when the shorter is and every closure is unchanged.

chooseAttachment (lower/shapes/attach) is read only for its form: without the pipelinedOnly guard a child under exact parents still pipelines, and a pipelinedOnly child under rows that read a search is refused by the checker first (check/approximate/attach.ts pipelinedOverSearch), so no admitted query fuses differently.

An ignored node's reasons (lower/optimize/dedup/explain.ts nodeReasons) feed only the plan's decisions and its Multiplicity diagnostics, which no code of the engine or the shell reads: a QueryTemplate carries its diagnostics and nothing renders them.

Without the reserved test (check/checker.ts services), a search source reading a label the checker reserved is refused UnsupportedOperation at the same stage all the same: a read of the enclosing rule's region is an outer read, which outerRefusal (check/approximate) refuses, and no description puts a recursion's self source inside a search, which the decoder refuses outside a recursive step; only the wording differs.

keyedOn's empty column set (lower/shapes/take) is keyed exactly when the empty key holds, where the physical analysis already bounds the source's maxCard by one (analysis/physical/rules.ts finish), so the bound differs only between at most zero and at most one rows; the take's shape reads it only against lateralMax and as a factor floored at one, so no shape changes.
The conservative nearest search (lower/conservative/vector) orders by its score first; listing the score again among the tie columns after it orders nothing the first key did not.

The hash index candidates of a reverse index (laws/model/plan.ts): a planned column is a field or a law column, so taking every column after the fields instead of the law columns alone lists the fields again, none of them hashable once the first pass found none, and then the law columns in their order: find returns the same column.

The rostered discriminant of a heterogeneous union (check/checker.ts) tried with no closed-id column: clashes over no column holds, since every arm's tuple over no column is the empty tuple and a heterogeneous union has two groups of at least one arm each, so the discriminant falls back to the literal columns as when the empty list is skipped.

uniqueBesideKey's test that an object compares every primary-key field (write/put/choose.ts) never decides: an installed unique object besides the arbiter that reads only primary-key fields and compares every one of them would hold apart only facts of one primary key, and none is installed (a key over a selected side of the whole primary key installs no object of its own: test/unit/write/put/choose.test.ts sees its MERGE either way), while one reading a field outside the key made the put the pair (candidateKey) first.

An axis pair repeating a base pair (laws/model/plan.ts carried pairs) at the target base's first column: no axis carries one, since a riding containment's carried pairs are those after the axis key (theory/families.ts ridesOf) and a fold's and a tree's pairs are their own columns, so the skip never fires at any index, and a pair whose target is a base column with another source is refused either way.

#lateNegations (check/checker.ts) without its early return for a rule with no negation returns no late negation instead of none: the early path then negates nothing and the late loop runs over nothing, so the head stands as built either way, and the slots it reads on the way are pure lookups.

directReads (write/schedule/plan.ts) with nothing carried walks the member's inputs (inputsOf, edgesOf deduplicated) and collects every Base relation, which is meta.reads, a Base's relation and its inputs' (ir/dag.ts relNode); its one reader asks only whether a written relation is among them.

The ledger's privileges (deploy/diff/diff.ts, ledger.ts ledgerPrivilegesObject) are one grant of SELECT on the ledger to every login's role: revoking it from every role the source granted and granting the target's to its roles leaves the roles the target names holding it and no other, as revoking it only from the roles the target drops does, inside the migration file's one transaction.

A readable identity's label (deploy/render/naming.ts label) keeping the dot after its schema: the label feeds only changeMigrationName, whose words fold every run of other characters into one underscore, so the dot joins the one after the verb and the name is unchanged.

decideFolder's order check (deploy/ledger/ledger.ts) refusing a folder that sorts before the last complete one but not one that sorts at it: a folder named as a complete folder is decided by the complete folders' lookup first, so no folder reaching the check shares the last one's name.

The ledger rows statement's output names (deploy/ledger/ledger.ts, c0 to c6 instead of c1 to c7): the migrate runner reads its rows by position (adapter/migrate/ledger.ts ledgerRowOf), so no reader names them.

admitsArity admitting no operand to a variadic native (scalar/compute/registry.ts) never decides: a variadic native enters an expression only through overloadOf, whose admits refuses an empty operand list, and every rewrite keeps an expression's arity (ir/expr.ts), so the lowering's arity tests never meet zero operands.

The owned clause of a set-aside relation's marker (deploy/diff/diff.ts ownedAside) when it owns nothing: every table grizzle installs has a primary key, which its own index carries, and every materialized view a unique index, its inherited key, which its concurrent refresh needs, so a table or a materialized view set aside always owns a key or an index (diff/aside.ts ownedBy) and the clause is always due.

The tables whose row security an installation enables, which the drift check meets with a role's filtered tables (deploy/admission/roles.ts roleExpectation secured): an installation creates a policy only beside its table's ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (physical/ddl/roles.ts addRowSecurity), so every filtered table is among the tables whose row security is enabled, which are among the tables altered at all; met with the filtered tables, either set gives the filtered tables.

Whether a default privilege's revoke names one of PostgreSQL's own defaults' grantees (deploy/admission/roles.ts sameGrantee): its second grantee is always a built-in default's, PUBLIC, so a revoke naming a role answers false whether or not the role's name is compared.

The AVG(money) refusal's test (scalar/aggregate.ts unaryOverload) without its name: sumOverloads defines a sum over money, so an aggregate over money with no overload is a mean, and the branch fires for exactly the calls it did.

Which of PostgreSQL's own default privileges an installation's revokes leave (deploy/admission/roles.ts defaultPrivilegesExpectations): every manifest that alters a default privilege is an installation's, whose PUBLIC revokes (physical/ddl/roles.ts publicRevokes) take ALL on functions and on types from PUBLIC everywhere, both of the defaults, so none is left whether or not each revoke is read.

A boolean literal typed by a named type called boolean (sql/print.ts printLiteral), printed bare instead of cast: the one named type a boolean literal takes is a contract's domain over boolean, whose predicate the host checks every literal against when it is built, so the cast adds no check, and PostgreSQL coerces a bare boolean into the domain wherever the literal is stored, compared or delivered, both readings of the same values.

Whether an input nothing proves holds no repeated row (write/insert/input.ts unproved), the proof of a described member read through a carrier or by an entry's outside check: a carrier holds its member's rows as a set after their casts into the relation's types (write/carriers/carriers.ts memberRows, SELECT DISTINCT unless the member's lowering is a set and every cast keeps its value), so a DISTINCT over it removes nothing, and an outside check reads a member only to find whether some row lies outside its entry, which a repeated row cannot change.
